title: fix(multiaxis): start and exit picks for the multi-axis contour
body:
## What changed

The Multi-Axis Contour (`OpType::MultiAxisContour`, the drive-curve planner `multiaxis::contour_curve`) takes a start point and an exit point. This is slice 2 of #3330. Slice 1 (the 5-Axis Contour) is PR #4006.

The title uses `fix`: the issue has the `bug` label, and PR #4028 used `fix` for the same reason.

Behaviour (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/curve_seam.rs`, hook in `contour_curve_seamed`):

- Each pick acts on the drive curve nearest it. The other curves keep their automatic cut. The cut order of the curves does not change.
- A pick with a Z is read in 3D. A pick without a Z is read in XY.
- Closed curve, start: the curve starts at its point nearest the pick. A foot between two vertices becomes a new vertex on that segment.
- Closed curve, exit: the curve cuts its full lap from its seam. Then it runs on along its own points to its point nearest the exit pick, and the tool leaves there.
- Open curve: the start pick selects the end where the cut starts (the nearer end). The exit pick selects the end where the cut leaves. The direction of the curve can reverse.
- The re-sequence occurs before the walk. Thus the rest law, the tilt limit (`command_axis` in the max-tilt cone) and the shank dodge judge each station of the picked path, as on the automatic path. The app's centre-cut audit (`audit_posed`) and the verify pass also read the picked path.
- The kind has no leads, so there is no lead-room law.
- With no pick, `apply` returns before it touches the curves. The path is byte-identical.
- `PickCapability::Ring` for the kind. The MCP `edit_operation` schema says how the kind reads a pick.

## Refusals (by name, before any motion)

- `start point (x, y): the nearest drive curve stands D mm away, farther than R mm (1.5 tool diameters) - ...` (also for the exit).
- `start point (...): drive curve N is open and its cut can start only at an end; its nearest end (...) stands D mm away, farther than R mm - ...` (also for the exit: `leave only at an end`).
- `exit point (...): it is nearer the end of open drive curve N where the start point begins the cut - ...`.
- `start point (...): the plunge column over drive curve N at (x, y, z) crosses the part - ...` and `exit point (...): the retract column over drive curve N at (...) crosses the part - ...`. The column law sweeps the ball up the vertical line to the hop plane, every 0.25 mm, and it checks the shank at each step when shank avoidance is on.

## Mutations

Each mutation was applied alone, the pins were run, and the source was restored.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `curve_seam::rotate` keeps the automatic seam (start seat off) | RED: `curve_start_point_seats_a_closed_curve_at_the_pick`, `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick`, `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M2 | `run_on`: the full lap dropped (the exit becomes a chord) | RED: `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick` |
| M3 | the plunge column check off (`curve.rs`) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | the retract column check off (`curve.rs`) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | open curve: the start reversal off | RED: `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends`, `curve_pick_acts_on_its_nearest_curve_only`, `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`; app: `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name` |
| M6 | open curve: the exit reversal off | RED: `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends` |
| M7 | the same-end exit refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M8 | the open start end reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M9 | the open exit end reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M10 | the curve reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M11 | the column sweep reads only the station (no samples up the column) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| A1 | the app arm passes an empty seam | RED: `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name` |
| A3 | the kind's capability back to `PICK_OWED` | RED: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick`, `multiaxis_contour_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` |

## Readings

- The pins that say "the cut geometry does not change" sample each cut move every 0.25 mm in both directions. Each sample of the picked path must be within 0.02 mm of the automatic ball-centre path (no chord, no gouge). Each sample of the automatic path must be within 0.02 mm of the picked path (no part of the curve left uncut). The walk's chord budget is 0.0025 mm.
- Box 40 x 40 x 15, ring at z = 7.5, ball r = 3: the start pick (20, -1) gives a first ball centre at (20.0, -3.0, 7.5) within 0.05 mm. The exit pick (-1, 20) gives a last ball centre at (-3.0, 20.0, 7.5).
- A canopy slab at z 18 to 20 above the middle of the y = 0 wall: a pick under it is refused for the plunge and for the retract. A pick on the x = 0 wall cuts.

## Pinning tests

- motion `multiaxis` (module `curve_seam`): `curve_start_point_seats_a_closed_curve_at_the_pick`, `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick`, `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends`, `curve_pick_acts_on_its_nearest_curve_only`, `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_without_a_pick_is_the_automatic_path_byte_for_byte`.
- app `start_exit_shared` (module `multiaxis_contour`): `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name`, `multiaxis_contour_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` (MCP `edit_operation`, `undo`, `redo`); and `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (updated).
- No new top-level test binary: the new files are modules of `multiaxis` and `start_exit_shared`.

## Goldens moved

None expected. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed.

## Not exercised

- A pick on a shank-avoid path where the shank, not the ball, blocks the column. The shank step uses the existing `shank_hits_at`; no pin drives it.
- A closed drive curve through the application (the app pins use the box's four open top edges). The closed curve is pinned at motion scale.
- A setup with a rotated frame: the picks and the drive curves are both in the setup frame, as for the 5-Axis Contour.

## Code shape

- `curve.rs` had 860 lines. Its unit tests moved, unchanged, to `curve_tests.rs`. It now has 719 lines, with the hook. A further split is a follow-up.
- No new crate edge.

## Remaining kinds of #3330

Parallel5D, Swarf, AdvancedSwarf, RotaryContour, RotaryParallel, RotaryOffset, MultiAxisRough, Flow5D.

## Gate

All on head `8d61b24d9` (local Mac):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 216 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.3 min). The plan includes `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: multiaxis`, `motion suites: pivot5d`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (14.4 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy step: none (P2).

Decision: `docs/decisions/3330-multiaxis-contour-picks.md`.

Effort: max.

Changelog: The Multi-Axis Contour takes a start point and an exit point: each pick re-sequences the drive curve nearest it, and an impossible pick is refused by name.
